text: The cutover is read once from a legacy Workbench cutover dump at the cutover window, on a read-only identity granted for it, in a layout agreed at the cutover rehearsal; the ten day rows, the reconciliation extract they came from and the data steward's sign-off are held in the cutover record of the release pipeline and not in a schema table, and the read-only window of the legacy tables is carried in that record as the retention period of the legacy tables.
why: AC3 needs a place for the ten clean days and the sign-off and a source for the extract, and no source gives the dump layout, the step name or the cutover record format; the story states the mechanism rather than inventing a value.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-005 AC3 and Endpoints; FSD P1 v3 A2.11 and A2.12; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 32 (one-off bulk work, no direct schema access); TSD P1 v3 T3.6
confirm: Data steward and the release pipeline owner at the cutover rehearsal.
impact: If the record moves into a table or the pipeline names its step differently, one evidence reader, one fixture and the state table change; no schema, contract or event change.

text: A migrated interaction carries the ACE business keys it holds as business keys and resolves nothing: person_key and contact_key are kept as the ACE customer and contact keys the legacy row holds, the ledger's party_id and contact_point_id cross-references stay as the ledger defines them for rows created by the application, and no party or contact identifier is minted for a legacy row that never had one.
why: The legacy data row names the two business keys while the ledger table defines two cross-references and no column of either name, so the load has to state where the keys go without inventing an identifier.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-005 Data table (interaction id, case_id, person_key, occurred_at, channel, direction and 25 more); TSD P1 v3 T3.3 views 3 and 4 and T1.1 boundary rule (business keys, no foreign key into ACE); FSD P1 v3 A1.1 constraints
confirm: Data architect with the data steward in the DP05 data product review.
impact: If the dictionary adds the two key columns or fixes source_ref as their home, one mapper field list and one fixture change; no table, event or workflow change.

text: The cutover load of contact_point_ext stays with the DP05 contact and promise slice that holds the rows, written by this story at the same time and in the same transaction as the interaction rows, while DP02 Customer and party keeps the catalog entry for the extension table and RWB-P1-DM002-APP reads it and writes none of it.
why: The FSD files contact_point_ext under DP02 and gives DP05 only interaction, but the legacy data row of this key carries the consent and contact-quality rows, so one of the two stories has to load them and the load follows the rows.
read: FSD P1 v3 A2.2 (DP02 and DP05 rows); TSD P1 v3 T3.5 and T3.9; legacy RWB-DM-005 Data table (contact_point_ext fields DF-EXT-013 to DF-EXT-026)
confirm: Data steward with the DP02 owner in the data product review, and the rwb-source-data service owner.
impact: If the load moves to RWB-P1-DM002-APP, one loader step and one fixture set move between the two stories; the tables, the grant and the read path do not change.

text: A clean day is a business date on which JOB-04 writes no BREAK row for a migrated record and raises no new REC-05 orphan for it; a PASS day moves the consecutive count up by one, a BREAK row or a new orphan resets it to zero and names the day, and the sign-off is offered only at ten consecutive clean days.
why: AC3 counts ten clean days on the migrated records but no source defines a clean day, the counter or the reset, so the story fixes the mechanism and cites it instead of inventing a number.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-005 AC3; FSD P1 v3 A2.11.2 (REC-05, zero orphans, every one listed) and A2.13 (publish hold); TSD P1 v3 T3.6 (reconciliation_result and the REC-05 row); DL25
confirm: Data steward with the owner of RWB-P1-E1011-APP before the story's Done.
impact: A different clean-day rule changes the evidence reader and TC-DM-005-03 only; no schema, contract or event change.

text: The version of this story is applied on the next free number of the rwb_source_data Flyway sequence after the V0001 baseline and the view versions, it creates no schema object, and it runs behind the platform feature flag rwb.source-data.dm005-cutover-extract: off, the cutover step refuses to start and no row is written, while the migration still applies because it creates nothing.
why: DP-15 requires a per-service version for the cutover definition and TSD P1 v3 T3.2 fixes only the sequence and the first versions, so the number and the switch need a default that changes no schema object.
read: Template and Rules R5.5 DP-15 and R3 default ruling (feature flags, platform library); TSD P1 v3 T3.2; ADR-021
confirm: Solution architect and the platform flag owner in the version review of the service.
impact: A different flag name or number is one values-file line and one history description; no code, contract, table or event change.
